body.text: Grand Theft Auto VI launches to rave reviews and gamer acclaim
In short:
Grand Theft Auto VI has received glowing praise from critics and gamers after launching globally overnight.
The latest title from Rockstar Gaming is reportedly the most expensive game ever developed, and it is believed to have already recouped its estimated $2.2 billion investment.
Its review score on Metacritic currently sits at 99, on par with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Baldur's Gate 3.
Critics are calling Grand Theft Auto VI a masterpiece after the most expensive game ever created launched overnight.
Launching just past midnight AEDT, many gamers stayed up overnight to play.
As media embargoes were lifted, dozens of reviews were published, delivering almost universal praise.
Former ABC Good Game Spawn Point host Angharad Yeo said GTA VI "may actually live up to the hype".
"It is just so wonderfully crafted, so detailed and immersive to the point where I'm expecting things that I should expect from it," Yeo said.
"I think people will be playing this for weeks, if not months, if not years."
Fans of the series waited 13 years for the latest instalment, and after lengthy delays, unprecedented hype and pressure surrounded the release.
A National Broadband Network spokesperson said on the night of November 18 and in the early morning of November 19, traffic surged to reach 36.54 terabits per second.
"The most data we've ever moved in a single second," they said.
"That's enough data to download GTA VI at 212GB around 21 times. Every. Single. Second.
"The new record is about 20 per cent above baseline, and breaks the previous record set on Thursday 12 November."
Initial reviews dashed fears the game could never live up to that hype.
On Metacritic, a game review aggregating website, GTA VI has a score of 99, a rank shared only by 2023's Baldur's Gate 3 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998).
ScreenHub Australia gave the game four stars out of five, and reviewer Alice Clarke said: "At its core, GTA VI is a pretty good game.
"There are large sections where it is an absolutely epic game, and large sections that are boring and too limited," she said.
"However, after I pushed through the boring parts and it opened up enough to become a proper GTA title, it became worth it."
Former Australian pro-gamer Jamie Skella told ABC News Radio the release was more of a cultural phenomenon than a regular video game launch.
"It's so rich, it's alive,"
"They've really added just immense amounts of detail to the non-player-controlled characters, and the voice acting is phenomenal."
GTA VI is said to be the most expensive game ever developed, with an estimated budget of more than $2.2 billion.
Yeo said developer Rockstar Games had likely already made its money back.
"Reportedly, they've brought in $US1.5 billion [$2.21 billion] in worldwide revenue based just on the pre-sales," she said.
Mr Skella said "some 1.5 million Americans are probably skipping work today for it", joining many Australians who have booked time off.
Longtime fan Danny Cotter has booked four days off work so he can play it at launch.
"I've got full faith that it's going to blow me away," he said before the release.
Mr Cotter set his Xbox time to New Zealand, allowing him to access it hours earlier than other Australian gamers, and he played it until 4am AEST.
"I just woke up and I'm ready to play all day today,"
"I was very, very impressed with the prologue.
"There is a plot point that I will not spoil that I can see making the story and the journey far more emotional at times, which I am excited for."
Jack Hudson also set his system time zone to New Zealand and clocked six to seven hours on the game overnight.
"This iteration of the game I feel ticks so many boxes," he said.
"It's just been phenomenal."
Mr Hudson, who has 5,000 hours in the game's predecessor, GTA V, has loved the role-playing element of GTA VI.
He rates it as a strong 9.5 out of 10 and thanked his boss, Emma Lo Russo, for approving his time off.
Declan Higgins said he enjoyed the game so much he had to make a conscious effort to go to bed after 3am.
"It's been so good," Mr Higgins said.
CBS reported in August that there was even a US Army Unit offering four days of leave to play the game for service people who re-enlisted for a two to six-year term of service.
Mr Skella, asked if it was worth the wait, said his answer could only be: "Hell yeah."
Yeo said there was still "so much to do" in her play-through.
"If previous Rockstar games are anything to go by, there's going to be very, very long legs on this game," she said.
